name: Amazon MQ
oneLiner: The odd one out: you rent brokers by the hour and pay for storage - the messages themselves are free.
trap: There is no per-message or per-API charge at all, so an idle broker costs exactly what a saturated one costs. Active/standby and 3-node cluster deployments multiply the instance hours.

name: Amazon API Gateway
oneLiner: REST and HTTP bill per request; WebSocket bills per message plus every minute a socket stays open.
trap: HTTP APIs meter in 512KB increments and WebSocket in 32KB increments, so one big payload is several billed units. WebSocket connection minutes accrue on idle sockets with zero traffic.

name: AWS AppFlow
oneLiner: A flat charge per flow run plus a charge per GB moved - your schedule frequency drives the bill.
trap: Billed per flow run, so cadence dominates: a 1-minute schedule is roughly 43k runs a month. Accelerated transfers count each concurrent process as an additional flow run.

name: AWS AppSync
oneLiner: Pay per GraphQL operation, per real-time update pushed, and per minute clients stay subscribed.
trap: Real-time messages meter per 5KB of payload, not per message - an 8KB update bills as two. Connection minutes tick while a subscriber sits idle, entirely separate from the updates.

name: Amazon Chime SDK
oneLiner: Attendee-minutes and messages dominate; phone numbers rent monthly.
trap: The Amazon Chime application hit end of support in February 2026. That did not touch the Chime SDK, which bills as normal. Separately, each provisioned DID costs a monthly rental at zero call volume.

name: Amazon Connect
oneLiner: Per-minute and per-message usage, plus a daily rent on every claimed phone number.
trap: People budget the per-minute voice rate and forget the number itself. A claimed DID or toll-free number accrues a daily charge until you release it back to inventory, even if nobody ever dials it.

name: Amazon Data Firehose
oneLiner: Billed on the bytes you push in, not the bytes delivered out - no shards and no hourly base charge.
trap: On Direct PUT each record rounds up to 5KB before billing, so a million 1KB records bill as 5GB, not 1GB. Format conversion and dynamic partitioning each add their own per-GB charge.

name: Amazon EventBridge
oneLiner: Custom events cost you on ingestion; AWS's own service events ride the default bus for free.
trap: Only custom and partner events bill - AWS management events ingest free. But a 200KB event is 4 billed events, since each 64KB chunk counts as one (8KB for Schema Discovery).

name: AWS IoT Core
oneLiner: Messages meter in 5 KB blocks; connection minutes tick on their own.
trap: An 8 KB publish bills as two messages and a 200 byte publish as one, so padding toward 5 KB is free but spilling past it is not. A triggered rule always meters at least one rule and one action, even if no action fires.

name: AWS IoT Device Management
oneLiner: Every fleet operation is a countable unit.
trap: Fleet indexing meters index updates in 1 KB chunks, so one fat shadow document reindexes as several updates each time it changes. Jobs bill per remote action delivered to a device, which multiplies across a large fleet.

name: AWS IoT Events
oneLiner: Active alarms bill by the month; inbound messages bill by evaluation.
trap: An alarm counts as active and bills for the month even if it never trips once, separate from the per-evaluation message charge. AWS has announced end of support for IoT Events, so nothing new should land here.

name: AWS IoT Greengrass
oneLiner: A core device that authenticates once in a month bills for that whole month.
trap: Only the core is metered. Devices talking to it over the local network cost nothing, but everything the core relays upward lands on IoT Core connection, messaging and shadow meters, which usually dwarf the per-core fee.

name: AWS IoT SiteWise
oneLiner: All three shapes at once: per-message ingest, GB-hour storage tiers, per-GB scanned on every query.
trap: ExecuteQuery bills by GB scanned, so a wide time window over a busy asset model can cost more than the ingest that produced the data. Hot tier storage meters by GB-hour and keeps running after the devices go quiet.

name: AWS IoT TwinMaker
oneLiner: Entities carry a monthly fee even when nobody opens the twin.
trap: Entity count is the sticky line. Model a plant at fine granularity and you create thousands of entities that bill every month, while queries and unified data access calls only bill when someone actually reads.

name: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
oneLiner: Provisioned pays shard-hours plus 25KB PUT units; on-demand pays a stream-hour plus GB in and out.
trap: The modes meter differently. Provisioned counts 25KB PUT payload units, so a 1KB record still bills as one full unit. On-demand bills per GB written - inbound is NOT free in this one.

name: Amazon Location Service
oneLiner: Per thousand requests across maps, places and routes, with stored geofences ticking monthly.
trap: A route matrix bills origins multiplied by destinations, so one call with 10 origins and 10 destinations is 100 routes. Asking for results you may store moves you onto a separate usage type costing several times more.

name: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
oneLiner: Kafka brokers by the hour plus storage; serverless swaps that for cluster-hours and partition-hours.
trap: Neither mode charges per message or per API call. Serverless bills every partition per hour, so an over-partitioned idle topic costs real money. Express brokers add a per-GB-written charge.

name: Amazon Pinpoint
oneLiner: You pay per endpoint targeted each month, plus per message on whichever channel actually sends.
trap: Monthly Targeted Audience bills every endpoint a campaign or journey touches, deliverable or not. AWS ends Pinpoint support on 30 Oct 2026 - SMS, voice and push move to End User Messaging.

name: Amazon SES
oneLiner: Outbound bills per recipient, not per message - a single blast to 50 addresses is 50 charges.
trap: One send to 50 recipients bills 50 times. Attachment bytes cost extra per GB, and inbound bills per email PLUS per 256KB received chunk, so a big attachment hits you twice on receive.

name: Amazon SNS
oneLiner: You pay to publish, then pay again for every delivery - one message to 10 subscribers is 11 charges.
trap: Fan-out double-charges: publish and each delivery bill separately, both chunked per 64KB. Deliveries to SQS and Lambda are free; HTTP/S, SMS and Firehose are not.

name: Amazon SQS
oneLiner: Every API action is a request - sends, receives, deletes, and empty polls all cost the same.
trap: Empty ReceiveMessage polls that return nothing still bill as requests, and payloads chunk: one 1 MiB call bills as 16 requests, not 1. Long polling is the fix.

name: AWS Step Functions
oneLiner: Standard bills per state transition; Express drops that and bills per start plus memory-seconds.
trap: Standard counts every transition including retries and each Map iteration - loops are not free. Express bills duration x memory instead, so a workflow that sits waiting burns GB-seconds.

name: Amazon WorkMail
oneLiner: Flat per-mailbox monthly seat, prorated by the hour.
trap: Billing tracks active user accounts, not logins. Deactivating a user mid-month earns no credit for the remaining days, and the 50 GB per user is bundled, so there is no separate storage meter.
